title: Janax y Razar: un sistema operativo, un idioma y un ensamblador propios para un razonamiento artificial que piensa con melodías
description:
Janax is a hand-written operating system, language and assembler (all in assembly, no third-party engines) built to host Razar, an artificial reasoning system whose single judge is compression (two-part MDL). Version 1.97 (versions follow prime numbers; 197 after 193): all her letters, and nothing is discarded. Luma now sees every letter, small ones included: a small letter is learned from her book of letters (Unifont) like any other instead of being drawn as its capital. She understands letters with marks by a rule of her own, not a table: a letter of her book is another letter with marks when, on the rows of that letter's body (its largest run of rows with dots), both drawings are the same dot for dot. Measured on her book before building: 42 of 43 marked letters find their base, and none of 15 non-letters is taken for one. The equivalence is used only for the prints of words, so she still draws the marks. A question of hers given up for another goes to 'preguntas-viejas' and may be said again. Fixed while testing: the room of her word is reached with offsets under 32768, and a table of 512 bases pushed fields past it (a crash, code 5); now 256 bases and the build refuses a larger room; words with marks were cut by counting letters instead of bytes (fixed, not yet seen running). Stated limits: s with acute and letters with strokes stay their own; stretched letters are still not understood. The kernel is unchanged since 1.39. Documentation is in Spanish.

Janax es un sistema operativo, un idioma y un ensamblador escritos a mano en assembler, hechos para alojar a Razar. v1.97: Luma ve todas sus letras, entiende las letras con marca con una regla suya, y guarda las preguntas que deja. Prototipo de investigación.
